v.rationale:
I ran all three test suites and they pass (26, 20 and 24 tests). I also ran a throwaway probe test in each implementation and then deleted it. It checked: a non-author sending an invalid payload, tag case, tags that differ only by whitespace, a null title on update, the CSRF behaviour outside the testing environment, a filter on an unknown tag, and a title that produces no slug.

impl-2 has a real production bug. Its API routes sit inside the 'web' middleware group, and with the environment switched out of testing, POST /api/posts returns 419 (CSRF). The suite hides this because Laravel skips CSRF checks during unit tests. It also has redundant trimming in prepareForValidation and an awkward UpdatePostRequest that extends StorePostRequest. That puts it clearly last.

impl-1 and impl-3 are close and share the same two minor flaws:
- A non-author sending an invalid payload gets 422 instead of 403, because the controller authorises after validation.
- Tag names are case-sensitive, so 'PHP' and 'php' become two tags.

impl-1 ranks first. It has separate Store and Update FormRequests, uses $request->enum() for the status filter, binds routes by slug, and uses ??= in the observer so factories can override the slug and published_at. Its 26 tests are the most thorough. Its weaknesses are a duplicated postAttributes() helper and an unnecessary Http::preventStrayRequests() in the tests.

impl-3 is a close second. Its nullable scopes keep the controller free of conditionals, its collection pipeline dedupes tags neatly, and its factory-based tests (hasAttached, sequence) are excellent. It loses a little for branching one request on isMethod('POST'), the tryFrom((string)) cast where $request->enum() exists, and a syncTagNames that both saves the tags and returns the reloaded model.
